The Story Behind the Artwork

She is a daughter of Cronos, born into a world where time claims everything. Yet she holds a sacred fish in her hands—a symbol of life, fertility, and renewal—and offers it to eternity. Her gesture raises a familiar question: What would we give to protect what we love from the passage of time?

The Creative Process

Meet the Artist

Born in Havana, Cuba, in 1973, Héctor “Chino” Pérez is a contemporary Cuban visual artist based in Miami, Florida. He studied at the School of Design in Havana and continued his artistic education through advanced studies at the San Alejandro Academy of Fine Arts.

In the 1990s, a devastating automobile accident resulted in the loss of his right forearm. Until then, he had painted with his right hand. Rather than abandon his career, Pérez taught himself to paint with his left hand. This experience became a defining chapter in his life and continues to shape the depth, determination, and emotional strength found throughout his work.

With 38 years of artistic experience, Pérez has exhibited internationally in more than 65 group exhibitions and 15 solo shows. His works are held in private collections and institutional collections across the United States, Canada, Europe, Mexico, Latin America, and Asia. His art has been presented through galleries, international exhibitions, and both private and public auctions.

Beyond his studio practice, Pérez has been deeply committed to community engagement. He developed artistic projects and taught art therapy to children and young adults with disabilities in Cuba. He later collaborated with organizations supporting people with disabilities in Montreal, Canada. He was invited to London in 2003–2004. After years in Montreal, he relocated to Miami in 2015, where he is now based and founded Chino Art Estudio1.

Recent sales milestones include Toward Abundance, a work measuring 28 inches in diameter that sold for $13,400 at a private auction on Fisher Island, Florida, in 2025. In 2026, a 40 × 60 inch work from the Tablas series sold for $48,250 at a private auction in the Hamptons on Long Island, New York. His artistic practice continues to evolve through collections that explore memory, identity, transformation, and the passage of time.
